snp5.5:1.1: “I ask you, Fortunate One, please tell this to me, said venerable Mettagū,
snp5.5:1.3: I think you have true understanding, and a developed self -
snp5.5:1.4: how have these countless kinds of suffering
snp5.5:1.5: arisen for whoever is in the world?”
snp5.5:2.1: “You asked me about the origin of suffering,
snp5.5:2.3: as I know it I will declare it to you:
snp5.5:2.4: Because of clinging to a basis countless kinds
snp5.5:2.5: of suffering originate for whoever is in the world.
snp5.5:3.1: The foolish one, without wisdom, clings to a basis,
snp5.5:3.2: and comes to suffering again and again, the fool.
snp5.5:3.3: Therefore knowing this, do not cling to a basis,
snp5.5:3.4: seeing the birth and origin of suffering.”
snp5.5:4.1: “You have proclaimed to us what we asked you about, said venerable Mettagū,
snp5.5:4.2: another thing we ask, come on, please answer it:
snp5.5:4.3: How do the wise ones cross over the flood
snp5.5:4.4: of birth, old age, grief, and lamentation?
snp5.5:4.5: Please explain this to me, O sage,
snp5.5:4.6: for this Teaching has been understood by you.”
snp5.5:5.1: “I shall proclaim the Teaching to you,
snp5.5:5.3: which is not hearsay in this world,
snp5.5:5.4: which, having understood, and living mindfully, one can cross over clinging to the world.”
snp5.5:6.1: “I greatly rejoice in that supreme Teaching, great seer,
snp5.5:6.3: which, having understood, and living mindfully, one can cross over clinging to the world.”
snp5.5:7.3: above, below, and across the middle,
snp5.5:7.4: dispel the enjoyment of, and settling on, these things,
snp5.5:7.5: and consciousness, and one will not remain in existence.
snp5.5:8.1: Living in this way, mindful, and heedful,
snp5.5:8.2: the monk who lives on after giving up loved things,
snp5.5:8.3: can, being wise, give up birth, old age,
snp5.5:8.4: grief, lamentation, and suffering right here.”
snp5.5:9.1: “I greatly rejoice in this, the Great Seer’s word, said venerable Mettagū,
snp5.5:9.2: O Gotama, well proclaimed is freedom from cleaving.
snp5.5:9.3: Surely the Fortunate One gave up suffering,
snp5.5:9.4: for this Teaching has been understood by you.
snp5.5:10.1: Surely they too can give up suffering,
snp5.5:10.2: whomever you would continually advise, O Sage,
snp5.5:10.3: therefore having met the Strong One, I revere him,
snp5.5:10.4: perhaps the Fortunate One could continuously advise me!”
snp5.5:11.1: “You should know the brahmin who has true understanding, Mettagū, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.5:11.2: who has nothing, and is not clinging to sense existence,
snp5.5:11.3: for he has surely crossed over the flood,
snp5.5:11.4: without hindrance or doubt, he has crossed beyond.
snp5.5:12.1: That man here who is wise, and has true understanding,
snp5.5:12.2: who has released the shackle of repeated existence,
snp5.5:12.3: he is craving-free, not troubled, not yearning -
snp5.5:12.4: he has crossed over birth and old age, I say.”
